newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board on Wednesday boosted by a large number of new share issues and listings on the domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 13.0 percent from 12.5 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell slightly to 2.6 million lots from 3.03 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Four companies issued or listed A shares on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchange on Wednesday and nine new A share firms will make their debut on the two bourses on Thursday.

"Big institutions including securities houses were seen borrowing heavily on the repo market today, especially in the seven-day contract," said one trader. "They need funds to trade the new A shares."
Traders said they expected the repo rates to keep on moving at the current high levels on Thursday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down in slow trading on Wednesday with the new A share issues sucking funds out of the market, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell slightly to 108.84 yuan from 108.85 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose slightly to 765,977 lots from a very thin 574,889 lots.

Traders said the market lacked liquidity after Beijing banned state banks trading on the exchange-based state debt markets, ordering them to trade instead on the local Chinese yuan interbank bank market based in Shanghai.
"Since the state banks withdrew from the spot market, daily volume has become thinner and thinner," a trader said.
"The heavy new A share issues have further sucked money out of the market," he added.
Traders said they expected the spot market to soon stabilise after weeks of downside trading.
